events.credibility_reason: Several F10 signals together: a claimed proof of a famous Landau problem with no engagement found in about a year; posted on preprints.ru, which reviews nothing; author with no established standing in analytic number theory; the later Chamberland–Straub review (Feb 2026) still treats the conjecture as open and does not cite it; the described method (comparing prime gaps with gaps between squares) is an elementary approach the problem is known to resist. The claim's content is known only from a search summary.
Claimed full proof of a landmark problem, about 7 years old, with no uptake; the 2026 review and Wikipedia still list the conjecture as open; unknown author; content known only from a search summary.

A large-n proof would itself be a landmark (beyond known short-interval results even under RH); 13 years with no uptake, not cited by later work, conjecture still treated as open in all large-n senses; titled as a full proof while abstract claims only large n; PDF unreachable, content only from a search summary.

why: Chamberland–Straub change the exponent (2+δ, δ>0) and assume RH, so they settle a variant, not the δ=0 statement. Sorenson–Webster is a finite verification (journal-published), i.e. instances. The three claimed proofs (Trushnikov whole, Sundarakannan whole, Goswami large-n case) are all set aside as not_credible: each is a claim on a landmark problem with long silence, no citation by later work, and the 2026 review still calling the conjecture open; Trushnikov adds a non-reviewing venue and an elementary method. The close call is Trushnikov: its text was never read, so not_credible rests on context signals rather than an identified error, and the claim itself is known only from a search summary. All 2025 dates fall wholly after 26 January 2024. No AI contributed mathematics to any event; Trushnikov's none_found false with empty systems still means none.
doubts: The record is an interim one written under an exhausted search quota (5 successful searches). None of the three claimed proofs was read; their content is from search summaries only. Pre-window analogues (Ingham, Baker–Harman–Pintz, Dudek) and AI-specific searches were not completed. The Sorenson–Webster bound's meaning (7·10^13 in n, n², or p) is unconfirmed but does not affect the instances call.
